units.text: The claim that Jefferson sent Livingston to join Monroe in France to negotiate for New Orleans in 1803 is supported by authoritative sources. X post and other sources confirm the dispatch and authorization for New Orleans negotiation.

citations.title: ArchaeoHistories on X: "Concerned about losing access to the port of New Orleans, in 1803 President Thomas Jefferson sent James Monroe and Robert Livingston to Paris to attempt to buy the city from France, authorizing them to offer France up to $10 million for it. judgement.reason: The passages state Jefferson sent/dispatched Livingston and Monroe to Paris in 1803 to negotiate for New Orleans, authorizing up to $10 million, so the X post and other sources confirm the dispatch and authorization.

units.text: Sources indicate the negotiation scope expanded beyond New Orleans to the entire Louisiana territory, and the final purchase price was approximately $15 million for the full territory, not just New Orleans.

citations.title: Robert R. Livingston’s Louisiana Purchase Letter | Historic New Orleans Collection

judgement.reason: The passage supports that the acquisition expanded from New Orleans to the entire Louisiana territory, but it does not mention the final purchase price of approximately $15 million.

units.text: One source notes Livingston's letter had not reached Jefferson by April 30, 1803, when the deal was already completed, which contradicts the claim's temporal priority but does not negate the 1803 dispatch.

citations.title: Robert R. Livingston’s Louisiana Purchase Letter | Historic New Orleans Collection

judgement.reason: The passage confirms the letter had not reached his superiors by April 30, 1803 when the deal was completed, but it does not specifically name Jefferson or address the 1803 dispatch claim.
